title: Binding affinities for 2D protein dimerization benefit from enthalpic stabilization
authors: Adip Jhaveri; Smriti Chhibber; Nandan Kulkarni; Margaret E Johnson
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD模拟研究BAR结构域蛋白在膜表面（2D）与溶液（3D）中的二聚化亲和力差异，聚焦蛋白-膜环境下的构象柔性对结合自由能的影响，虽非TF-DNA体系，但蛋白-蛋白二聚化结合建模与MD方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Dimerization underpins all macromolecular assembly processes both on and off the membrane. While the strength of dimerization, K D , is commonly quantified in solution (3D), many proteins like the soluble BAR domain-containing proteins also reversibly dimerize while bound to a membrane surface (2D). The ratio of dissociation constants, , defines a lengthscale that is essential for determining whether dimerization is more favorable in solution or on the membrane surface, particularly for these proteins that reversibly transition between 3D and 2D. While purely entropic rigid-body estimates of h apply well to transmembrane adhesion proteins, we show here using Molecular Dynamics simulations that even moderate flexibility in BAR domains dramatically alters the free energy landscape from 3D to 2D, driving enhanced selectivity and stability of the native dimer in 2D. By simulating BAR homodimerization in three distinct environments, 1) solution (3D), 2) bound to a lipid bilayer (2D), and 3) fully solvated but restrained to a pseudo membrane (2D), we show that both 2D environments induce backbone configurations that better match the crystal structure and produce more enthalpically favorable dimer states, violating the rigid-body estimates to drive h ≪ h RIGID . Remarkably, contact with an explicit lipid bilayer is not necessary to drive these changes, as the solvated pseudo membrane induces this same result. We show this outcome depends on the stability of the protein interaction, as a parameterization that produces exceptionally stable binding in 3D does not induce systematic improvements on the membrane. With h lengthscales calculated here that are well below a physiological volume-to-surface-area lengthscale, assembly will be dramatically enhanced on the membrane, which aligns with BAR domain function as membrane remodelers. Our approach provides simple metrics to move beyond rigid-body estimates of 2D affinities and assess whether conformational flexibility selects for enhanced stability on membranes.
abstract_zh: 二聚化是所有大分子组装过程的基础，无论是在膜上还是膜外。虽然二聚化的强度K D通常在溶液（3D）中量化，但许多蛋白质，如可溶性BAR结构域蛋白，在结合到膜表面（2D）时也会可逆地二聚化。解离常数之比定义了一个长度尺度，对于确定二聚化在溶液中还是膜表面上更有利至关重要，特别是对于这些在3D和2D之间可逆转换的蛋白质。虽然纯熵刚体估计的h适用于跨膜粘附蛋白，但我们在此通过分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟表明，即使BAR结构域具有中等程度的柔性，也会显著改变从3D到2D的自由能景观，从而在2D中增强天然二聚体的选择性和稳定性。通过模拟BAR同源二聚化在三种不同环境中的行为：1）溶液（3D），2）结合到脂质双层（2D），以及3）完全溶剂化但限制在伪膜上（2D），我们表明两种2D环境都诱导了更匹配晶体结构的骨架构象，并产生更有利的焓二聚体状态，违反了刚体估计，导致h ≪ h RIGID。值得注意的是，与显式脂质双层的接触并非驱动这些变化所必需，因为溶剂化的伪膜也产生了相同的结果。我们表明这一结果取决于蛋白质相互作用的稳定性，因为一种在3D中产生异常稳定结合的参数化在膜上并未诱导系统性改进。根据此处计算的h长度尺度远低于生理体积与表面积之比，膜上的组装将显著增强，这与BAR结构域作为膜重塑器的功能一致。我们的方法提供了简单指标，以超越2D亲和力的刚体估计，并评估构象柔性是否选择性地增强膜上的稳定性。
